entries.sourceChart: US App Store Top Free Games #2 (observed Oct 2026)
entries.why: Its spatial drag-the-block-to-the-matching-door loop, played against a timer, is hugely addictive. Night Arcade only had atmospheric horror exploration, so a polished casual puzzle rounds out the catalog.
entries.notes: v1 (2026-10-06) used swipe-to-slide 1x1 crates, which was too loose. v2 rework (2026-10-06) follows the source's core loop much more closely. Crates are multi-cell shapes moved with direct drag. Each color has edge bay doors, and a crate passes only if every row or column it covers fits inside the door span. There is a per-level countdown with no move limit, plus unlimited undo. Obstacles map to genre staples under our own fiction: frost (ice/freeze counter), rail (one-axis arrows), shrink-wrap (multilayer), roller shutter (locked/color shutter), and bollards and voids (irregular boards). Boosters are Break (freeze the clock 10s) and Lift (remove one crate), with one +30s overtime on fail. There are 18 handcrafted bays, all checked by tools/solve.js. Own name, fiction (night freight dock), art (procedural canvas crates), audio (WebAudio synth) and copy. No Block Out names, assets, characters or trademarked terms are used.

v3.notes: Feel pass after playtest feedback that input was less tactile than the source. Added magnetic one-axis rails with hysteresis and aligned corner turns, a sine detent at cell lines, 1:1 finger tracking, momentum flicks with friction, swept collision, spring settle, impact squash, cell-crossing haptic ticks, and accelerating suck-out through doors. Level rules and content are unchanged.

entries.sourceChart: US App Store Top Free Games #1 (observed 2026-10-07 via itunes.apple.com/us/rss/topfreeapplications/genre=6014)
entries.why: It's the #1 free game in the US right now (about 295k ratings at 4.8). It's a pure deduction grid puzzle in the region-queens family, which adds real variety next to Night Arcade's horror exploration and block-escape titles. Its loop of tap to cross out, double-tap to commit, and a 3-heart mistake budget translates faithfully into a zero-dependency canvas game.
entries.notes: Core loop kept close to the source. It uses an n×n board with n colored regions, one piece per row, column, and region, and no two pieces touching (8-neighborhood). Every board has a unique solution solvable by logic. Single tap toggles a cross, drag paints or erases crosses, and double-tap commits a piece. A correct piece locks and can't be removed, and a wrong commit costs one of 3 lives. At 0 lives you can retry, or take one revive (the source uses a rewarded ad; ours is free). The game has a count-up timer with best time, Undo / Hint / Reset buttons, and a hint that first flags mistakes and then explains a forced move. The campaign mixes sizes from 5×5 to 10×10 non-monotonically, and there's a daily puzzle with a streak. Original elements are the name, fiction (owls roosting in moonlit groves of the Hush Wood), lives as moons, the procedural canvas owl art, WebAudio hoots and ticks, and the copy. Additions for feel include magnetic row/column rails on drag-paint, a press squash and spring, X stamp overshoot, owl drop-and-squash, an auto-cross ripple outward from each owl, eyes that track the finger, and haptic ticks. No source names, cats, art, audio, logos, or trademarked terms are used in the game or catalog.
